Progress rail

.dr-node · --done · --now · .dr-rail · --at2 · --zone · __step · __lbl · __lbl--now · components/progress.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

  • Accepted
  • En route
  • On‑site
  • Done
  1. 1.dr-railA 4-column grid. The 2px track runs behind the circles from the centre of column 1 to the centre of column 4 (12.5%, 75% wide), --border-hairline for the rail and green for the walked span. The walked span's width is --dr-fill.
  2. 2.dr-node--doneA finished milestone: green fill and border, charcoal check, 9.46:1.
  3. 3.dr-node--nowThe live milestone: green border, a charcoal dot on the card ground and a 4px halo of green at 20%.
  4. 4.dr-rail__lbl--nowThe live label steps from slate 11/400 to charcoal 11/600, so the state is carried by glyph, weight and position, never colour alone.
  5. 5li:last-child .dr-nodeA pending milestone: 22px circle, 2px --border-hairline border on --bg-surface, no glyph.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: (.dr-node, .dr-rail) — the order card's rail and the tracking timeline.

States

No state of its own: the rail reports where the order is, and nothing in it takes focus. In the order card it stands inside the card's link, which carries the states: see order card.

When to use

The rail answers the question the client asks most between payment and arrival: where is my order now. It closes the void RJ-C2 names, so it stands wherever a live order is shown: the active card on order-history and the Progress zone of tracking, its -aerial / -inspection variants and their empty and error states. tracking-loading draws no rail. One node component serves both places.

The milestones are the canonical four everywhere: Accepted · En route · On-site · Done. Labels are one or two words, the user's words for where the order is, never equipment terms. On‑site takes a non-breaking hyphen so the shortest label cannot break and shift the rail. aria-current="step" marks the live step programmatically, so WCAG 1.4.1 is met by glyph, weight and position. Every screen shows step 2 of 4, En route.

The rail is horizontal only. No screen builds a vertical axis and no class for one is declared in components/.

Sources: wireframes/tracking.html, order-history.html · DESIGN.md § Progress · voice.md P1, P4 · components/progress.css · CLAUDE.md RJ-C2

Rule and anti-rule

Do

  • Accepted
  • En route
  • On‑site
  • Done

The four milestones of one live order on tracking, with the current one marked by aria-current="step", its own dot and a heavier label.

Don’t

  • Service
  • Details
  • Pay
  • Track

The rail as a checkout stepper. It tracks the order's milestones and nothing else; a rail that counts form steps teaches the client that the four nodes mean something other than where the operator is. The ordering flow is three taps and needs no stepper. For a position among slides, use the pager.
